## Fire Decision + EKF Consumption — Ground Truth

### TL;DR
- **Is the EKF dead code in the alarm path?** No, but it is only *partially* alive. `EkfPublicState.s` (fused arc-length position) **does** drive `progressMeters` on metro legs / degraded / metro mode (`trackingservice.dart:1176-1185`), which feeds metro stop-counting and metro time ETA. `_lastEkfState` is genuinely populated from the live EKF stream (`trackingservice.dart:2165-2167`). **However `EkfPublicState.v` and `EkfPublicState.sigmaS` are never consumed by the fire decision** — only logged/snapshotted. In surface (GPS-healthy non-metro) mode the EKF is bypassed entirely and firing is pure GPS.
- **Point estimate or pessimistic fractile?** Point estimate only. `sigmaEta` is computed by EtaEngine (`eta_engine.dart:536-548`) and then thrown away (no reader anywhere). There is **no `median - k*sigma <= lead` safety margin**. For a "must wake BEFORE the stop" product this is the single most important gap.

### (1) How each mode fires + position/velocity source
| Mode | Fire rule | Position source | Speed source |
|---|---|---|---|
| stops (metro) | geometric: `remainingStopsToTarget <= N` (`alarm_evaluator.dart:796-797`) | **EKF.s** on metro legs, else GPS snap | n/a |
| stops (non-metro) | 40%-progressed / 60% rule (`alarm_evaluator.dart:1105-1106`) | GPS snap | n/a |
| time (non-metro) | `smoothedETA <= N*60` (`alarm_controller.dart:680-682`) | GPS snap | smoothed **GPS** speed |
| time (metro) | `estimateEtaSecondsToMeters <= N*60` (`alarm_evaluator.dart:344-351`) | EKF.s | GPS speed, else scheduled step durations |
| distance | `total - progress <= N*1000`, else straight-line GPS (`alarm_controller.dart:514, 776, 447`) | GPS snap / raw GPS | n/a |

Note: `AlarmMode` has **3** values `{stops, time, distance}` (`alarm_evaluator.dart:6`) — the "4 modes" in the brief is not what the code implements; "minutes-before" and "time-before" are the same path.

### (2) EKF consumption verdict
- `EKF.s` → `progressMeters`: **CONSUMED**, gated to metro/degraded (`trackingservice.dart:1177-1185`).
- `EKF.v`: **NOT CONSUMED** in firing/ETA (grep empty). Speed is smoothed GPS (`alarm_controller.dart:580-582`, `eta_engine.dart:369`).
- `EKF.sigmaS`: **NOT CONSUMED** in firing; logged (`trackingservice.dart:2221`) and saved to snapshot (`location_stream_handler.dart:403`).

### (3) Safety margin
None uncertainty-based. Only ad-hoc ETA-inflation heuristics exist: `speedSafetyFactor=1.20` (`alarm_evaluator.dart:1417,1441`) and step floor factor 0.60–0.90 (`eta_engine.dart:488-503`). These bias the point estimate; they are **not** sigma-scaled fractiles and do not use EKF.sigmaS.

### (4) Eligibility gate
- Time non-metro: `moved>=100m && etaSamples>=3 && >=30s` (`location_stream_handler.dart:602-604`, enforced `alarm_controller.dart:623-634`).
- **Metro time bypasses the gate** (`alarm_controller.dart:626`).
- **Stops and distance: no minimum-time gate** — can fire first tick; only `firedLegIds` / destination-fired dedupe them.

### Why this matters for the sleeping-rider, tunnel, budget-phone scenario
On the metro leg the alarm rides on `EKF.s` with **zero position-error cushion** and fires on the **exact** stop count / median ETA. A single EKF arc-length error greater than one inter-station spacing, or a median-ETA that is 50/50 around the true arrival, fires the wake-up *late* — the exact failure mode the product cannot have. The infrastructure to fix it (sigmaEta, EKF.sigmaS, EKF.v) is already computed and simply needs to be plumbed into the fire decision.

Scope: how the app models multi-leg journeys/transfers, detects wrong-direction, handles mid-journey deviation/reroute (incl. offline), and behaves under express trains. EKF filter math intentionally not audited; EKF behavior cited only where it surfaces (or hides) journey-shape signals.

### 1. Multi-leg journeys & line transfers — IMPLEMENTED (robust)
- Per-leg model: `TransferUtils.extractTransitLegStops` (`lib/services/transfer_utils.dart:880-1081`) builds one `TransitLegStops` per transit step with cumulative leg-start/end meters, per-stop meters, `lineName`, `isMetro`, and coalesces fragmented walk steps by stable name (`1038-1072`).
- Transfer/boarding events: `buildRouteEvents` (`transfer_utils.dart:382-715`) emits `preBoarding`, `transfer`, `mode_change`. The **walk-between-platforms** case is handled explicitly: METRO→WALK→METRO within ~600m is classified as an "interchange walk" and suppressed as a spurious "start walking" event (`499-563`), with 400m event de-dup (`703-714`).
- Stop truth for India: `enhanceTransitLegStopsWithOsm` (`1164-1394`) ignores Google `num_stops` and derives intermediate stops from bundled OSM `allIndiaStops` within 500m of the transit polyline, incl. a "Mumbai fix" so next-leg platform stops don't leak into the current leg (`1281-1319`). This is offline-capable and India-first.
- Alarms per leg: `alarm_evaluator.dart` fires transfer/preBoarding/switch-point alarms for both stops- and time-mode.
- Setup-time guard: `StopLogicEngine.validateThresholdAgainstMetroLegs` (`lib/services/stop_logic_engine.dart:218-295`) rejects a stops threshold ≥ the shortest metro leg's stop count.

### 2. Wrong-direction — MISSING / silently clamped (SHOWSTOPPER)
There is no wrong-direction feature anywhere in `lib/`. Off-route logic is lateral-offset-only (`deviation_detection.dart:60-66`, `deviation_monitor.dart:52-123`), so a reverse rider on the same corridor never trips deviation. Progress can't self-correct: `snap_to_route.dart:172` (+100 "Hard resistance to backward movement") and `:202-204` (+50 reverse-lane penalty), and on **every metro leg** `ekf_pipeline.dart:204-208` hard-clamps `if(_v<0)_v=0; if(_s<sOld)_s=sOld;` (metro leg forces `setAllowReverse(false)` at `ekf_orchestrator.dart:288`). Result: a sleeping rider who boards the opposite-direction metro at an interchange has **progress frozen at the boarding point** — the destination alarm never reaches threshold and no wrong-way warning ever fires. This directly breaks the "wake before the stop" promise and confirms the prior science session's silent-reverse-clamp claim in production code.

### 3. Mid-journey deviation & reroute — PARTIAL, offline-suppressed
Wired end-to-end: `DeviationMonitor` → band logic (`route_session_manager.dart:1114-1130`: 100–150m = local switch, >150m sustained = reroute) → `ReroutePolicy` → `TrackingService._handleRerouteDecision` (`trackingservice.dart:1311-1460`) → `RerouteConstraints.validate` → register-or-terminate.
- **Offline reroute is fully suppressed** (`reroute_policy.dart:39-52`; also aborted at `trackingservice.dart:1368-1376` when `offlineCoordinator.isOffline`) — i.e., dead during tunnel stretches, the core use case.
- Metro deviation is effectively inert (EKF-clamped progress + rider stays on shared corridor → low offset), and non-metro deviation reroute is an open TODO (`trackingservice.dart:1169`). So reroute mostly protects road/walk legs.
- The online/offline gate for `ReroutePolicy` is pushed only from the **foreground** HomeScreen connectivity listener (`homescreen.dart:78-93` → `TrackingService.setOnline` `:2444`); screen-off/backgrounded for hours can leave `_online` stale.

No schedule/real-time/express detection exists (grep confirms; `eta_engine.dart:26` is a *synthetic* dwell model). Because express follows the same track:
- **Stops-mode** degrades gracefully — stops are counted by geographic meters passed (`transfer_utils.dart:157-172`), so passing each stop location still increments the count.
- **Time-mode** breaks — ETA comes from planned/synthetic durations, so a faster-than-planned express makes the "N min before arrival" alarm fire **late** (product-killing). No mechanism reconciles planned vs observed speed.

`deviation_detection.dart` (incl. its `isOffline ? 1500 : 600` threshold at `:50-57`) has **no production caller** (grep). The live path is `DeviationMonitor`, which has no offline widening — so off-route tolerance does NOT actually relax offline despite that file suggesting it does.

1. Wrong-direction detection + stop silent metro-progress clamp (SHOWSTOPPER).
2. Observed-speed ETA for time-mode / express (HIGH).
3. Background-driven, non-suppressed offline reroute + non-metro reroute TODO (HIGH).
4. Remove/repurpose dead deviation_detection.dart (LOW).

## Android Background Survival — Ground-Truth Audit

**Scope:** lib/services/tracking/*, lib/services/trackingservice.dart, lib/services/notification_service.dart, lib/services/permission_service.dart, android/ native side. EKF math excluded per instructions.

### Verdict: FRAGILE. Real survival odds for a 2h screen-off journey on a Xiaomi/Samsung phone with the app swiped away: LOW.

The foreground service is *configured* correctly for Android 14 (FGS type declared + matching runtime perms), and there is a snapshot-based OS-restart recovery path. But every proactive OEM-kill mitigation is missing, and — most importantly — the alarm's actual sound/notification delivery is structurally broken in the one scenario the product exists for (app swiped away, phone in pocket, rider asleep).

### Science-session claims — verified against code

| Claim (science session) | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| D1: no WAKE_LOCK anywhere | **CONFIRMED (missing)** | zero hits for WAKE_LOCK/PowerManager in android/ + lib/; no wakelock dep in pubspec.yaml |
| D1: no REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS | **CONFIRMED (missing)** | not in AndroidManifest.xml (lines 3-13); permission_service.dart never requests it |
| D2: trackingservice autoStart:false | **CONFIRMED** | trackingservice.dart:212 (Android), :220 (iOS) |
| D2: AlarmReceiver.kt empty / no BOOT_COMPLETED | **CONFIRMED** | AlarmReceiver.kt = 0 bytes; no `<receiver>` and no RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED in manifest |
| D3: heartbeat pauses/stops tracking on UI death | **PARTIAL** | heartbeat_monitor.dart:45-98 sets paused flag + swaps notification to "Tracking paused" + stops its own timer, but does **not** stop GPS or alarm evaluation |

### Android 14 foreground-service type
**IMPLEMENTED correctly.** AndroidManifest.xml:52-54 declares `foregroundServiceType="location|mediaPlayback"`, backed by FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION and FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK (lines 9-10). Caveat: `mediaPlayback` has no backing MediaSession and background-location can be declined at runtime — either can cause the FGS start to be rejected on Android 14+ (see gaps).

### OEM-killer mitigation
**MISSING entirely.** No battery-optimization exemption request, no Doze wake lock, no OEM autostart guidance/deep-links, no boot receiver, no WorkManager/AlarmManager watchdog. The app leaves itself fully at the mercy of MIUI/Samsung/Oppo power management.

### The dominant real-world risk (beyond D1–D3)
`AlarmController.triggerAlarmNotification` (alarm_controller.dart:277-286) **delegates all alarm sound + notification to the UI isolate** via `service.invoke('triggerAlarm')` when running in the background isolate — it never shows the notification itself, and the sound is the in-process `AlarmPlayer` (notification_service.dart:795-796) with the notification set `playSound:false` (line 728). When the rider swipes the app away, the UI isolate/engine dies, the delegated invoke has no live listener, and the alarm is **silent and invisible** even though the foreground service and GPS loop are still alive. This is the single most product-killing gap and is independent of whether the OS kills the process.

### Recommended priority order for a solo/India-first founder
1. Fire the alarm (full-screen, channel-backed alarm sound) directly from the background isolate — do not depend on the UI isolate.
2. Request battery-optimization exemption + OEM autostart onboarding (permission_handler is already a dependency).
3. Hold a partial wake lock around active tracking / alarm firing.
4. Add a BOOT/WorkManager watchdog (or explicitly document OS-restart-only recovery).
5. Stop mislabelling swipe-away as "paused."

## Alarm Delivery — Ground-Truth Audit

**Verdict: FRAGILE.** When the app's UI isolate is alive (phone merely backgrounded, screen off, app still in memory), delivery is actually strong: alarm-stream audio, insistent looping sound, full-screen intent, screen wake, vibration on the alarm usage channel, and a sensible one-shot latch. **But for the product-critical scenario — a 2h sleeping journey, screen off, app process killed by an aggressive OEM (Xiaomi/Samsung), possibly in a metro tunnel — the design has two showstopper single points of failure and no independent backstop.**

### How the alarm is raised
- Notification: `flutter_local_notifications` on `geowake_alarm_channel_v4`, Importance.max/Priority.max, `category=alarm`, `fullScreenIntent:true`, `audioAttributesUsage=alarm`, `ongoing`, FLAG_INSISTENT + FLAG_NO_CLEAR (`notification_service.dart:721-769`). The channel itself has `playSound:false`.
- Sound: separate `audioplayers` stream, `USAGE_ALARM` + `stayAwake` + looping (`alarm_player.dart:13-24,53`). Because it uses the ALARM usage/stream, it **plays over ringer-silent and vibrate** — good. DND "Total Silence" is **not** handled.
- Vibration: native waveform with `VibrationAttributes.USAGE_ALARM` (`MainActivity.kt`), Dart fallback (`alarm_haptics.dart`).
- Screen wake: `fullScreenIntent` + `USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT` + `showWhenLocked`/`turnScreenOn` (manifest). **targetSdk=34**, so FSI is OS-restricted and there is no `canUseFullScreenIntent()` check or grant flow.

### The two showstoppers
1. **Everything is delegated to a possibly-dead isolate.** Alarm evaluation runs only in the background service isolate, but `triggerAlarmNotification` there does *not* play/show anything — it fires `service.invoke('triggerAlarm')` (fire-and-forget, no ACK/retry) to the UI isolate, which does the actual `showWakeUpAlarm` (`alarm_controller.dart:277-286` → `foreground_bridge.dart:203-233` → `trackingservice.dart:150-166`). Kill the UI process and the alarm is silent. The bg re-post net (`ensureAlarmNotificationVisible`) is gated on `pending_alarm_flag`, which only the foreground ever sets — so it can't rescue a foreground that never ran.
2. **No exact-alarm backstop (science-session D2 confirmed MISSING).** No `AlarmManager`, `android_alarm_manager_plus`, `zonedSchedule`, or `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM`/`USE_EXACT_ALARM` anywhere. If the foreground service dies (Doze/OEM/crash/reboot), nothing fires. The only thing keeping the alarm alive is a GPS foreground service running continuously for 2 hours.

### Making it worse
- The **HeartbeatMonitor pauses tracking** when the foreground dies (`heartbeat_monitor.dart:45-91`) — it shows "Tracking paused" instead of arming a self-contained alarm. This turns the exact target scenario into a guaranteed silent miss.
- Android 14 FSI is unverified (no runtime grant flow) → screen may not wake.
- A single failed `show()` is swallowed with no retry/escalation (`notification_service.dart:827-835`).

### One-shot latch (as designed)
Confirmed intentional: `setDestinationAlarmFiredForKey` + suppression (`alarm_controller.dart:117-126,1075-1098`), reset in `resetAlarmState` (`:226-240`). Fires once; the looping insistent sound persists until Stop Alarm/End Tracking. Reasonable — the risk is not nagging, it's the delivery paths above.

### Minimum viable fixes (solo/budget, India-first)
1. Make the background isolate raise the alarm itself (notification + native sound/vibration) rather than delegating; keep foreground delegation only as an enhancement.
2. Add a native `AlarmManager.setAlarmClock()` backstop scheduled from ETA (Doze-exempt) so the alarm fires even if the whole tracking loop is dead.
3. Stop the heartbeat monitor from pausing on UI death; instead switch to bg-self-contained delivery / ensure the exact alarm is armed.
4. Verify FSI grant on Android 14 and offer DND-bypass setup.
